heading: Title Page

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 1 · Of Christian Oeconomie, and of the Familie.

items.text: Govern the household according to the written word of God.
items.quote: The onely rule of ordering the Family, is the written word of God.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: TO THE RIGHT HONORABLE ROBERT Lord RICH, Baron of Leeze, &c.

items.text: Govern your household in righteousness and the fear of God, for from it church and commonwealth take their frame.
items.quote: the holie and righteous gouernment thereof, is a direct meane for the good ordering, both of Church and Common-wealth

items.text: Govern your children with diligence, not indulging their faults, lest they become ungodly.
items.quote: It was the fault of the priuate gouernment of Eli the Priest, that made his sonnes Hophni and Phinehas, of vngratious children, vngodlie Church-men.

items.text: See that your family is founded in the fear of God and ordered by his revealed will, for only such receive his blessing.
items.quote: no Familie can bee interessed in the blessing and fauour of God, which is not founded in his feare, and ordered according to his reuealed will.

items.text: Learn subordination in the family, for he who is not framed to economic subjection will hardly bear civil obedience.
items.quote: the Inferiour, who is not framed to a course of Oeconomicall subiection, will hardly vndergoe the yoke of ciuill obedience.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: TO THE RIGHT HONORABLE ROBERT Lord RICH, Baron of Leeze, &c.

items.text: Seek the free and advised consent of your parents before marriage, for without it the marriage is null in the court of conscience.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, TO THE RIGHT HONORABLE ROBERT Lord RICH, Baron of Leeze, &c.
items.quote: Marriages consummate without the free and advised consent of Parents, either explicite in tearmes, or implicite by conniuence, are in the court of conscience, meere nullities.

items.text: Put away your spouse only for fornication; do not separate for any other cause, including a vow of chastity or holy orders.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, TO THE RIGHT HONORABLE ROBERT Lord RICH, Baron of Leeze, &c.
items.quote: Matrimonie lawfullie begun and consummate, is made voide only by way of diuorce in the case of Adulterie.

items.text: Let your virtues season your children in their young years, that they may yield increase of honor.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, TO THE RIGHT HONORABLE ROBERT Lord RICH, Baron of Leeze, &c.
items.quote: whose young yeeres being seasoned therein, by the sweete sauour of their fathers vertues

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 2 · Of the Household seruice of God.

items.text: Establish and settle the private worship and service of God in your household.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 2 Of the Household seruice of God
items.quote: he will commaund his sonnes and his household after him, that they keepe the way of the Lord

items.text: Teach your children the words and ordinances of God, and answer their questions about them.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 2 Of the Household seruice of God
items.quote: And thou shalt whet them vpon thy children, & talke of thē when thou tariest in thine house

items.text: Assemble with the household for morning and evening prayer before beginning your daily labors.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 2 Of the Household seruice of God
items.quote: the familie comming together in one place, is to call vpon the name of the Lord, before they begin the workes of their callings

items.text: Offer prayer and thanksgiving before and after meals, receiving food as sanctified by the word and prayer.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 2 Of the Household seruice of God
items.quote: before and after meales; For meats and drinkes are blessed to the receiuers, by the word and prayer

items.text: Join with the household in fasting when called by present or imminent calamity.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 2 Of the Household seruice of God
items.quote: fasting, which is (as occasiō serueth) to be vsed both publikely & priuately, especially when they of the familie be therunto called by some present or imminent calamitie

items.text: Employ yourself in honest and profitable business according to your ability to maintain the household's temporal estate.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 2 Of the Household seruice of God
items.quote: euery member in the familie, according to their abilitie, employ themselues in some honest and profitable businesse

items.text: Reveal any family member who departs from his calling and entices another to idolatry.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 2 Of the Household seruice of God
items.quote: if any one in the familie starteth aside out of his calling, and inticeth another to idolatrie, he is to be reuealed

items.text: Live in mutual love and agreement with your spouse.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 2 Of the Household seruice of God
items.quote: the mutuall loue and agreement of the Man and Wife

items.text: Obey your parents dutifully.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 2 Of the Household seruice of God
items.quote: the dutifull obedience of children to their parents

items.text: Serve your master faithfully.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 2 Of the Household seruice of God
items.quote: the faithfull seruice of seruants to their Masters

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 3 · Of maried folkes.

items.text: Yield subjection to him, as the lower to the higher.
items.quote: the other is lower, and yeeldeth subiection

items.text: Bear rule over her, as the higher over the lower.
items.quote: the one is alwaies higher, and beareth rule

items.text: Leave father and mother and cleave to your wife.
items.quote: shall a man leaue father and mother, and shall cleaue vnto his wife

items.text: Have only her as your one flesh; do not take another wife or concubine.
items.quote: two, and not three or foure, shall be one flesh

items.text: Be fruitful and multiply, filling the earth.
items.quote: Increase and multiplie and fill the earth

items.text: Raise up a godly seed for the church.
items.quote: he sought a godly seed

items.text: Do not deprive one another, except by mutual consent for a time of prayer and fasting.
items.quote: abstaine with consent for a time, that they might giue themselues to fasting and praier

items.text: Trust in her for household matters.
items.quote: The heart of her husband trusteth in her

items.text: Labor cheerfully with your hands for the household.
items.quote: She seeketh wooll, and flaxe, and laboureth cheerefully with her hands

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 4 · Of the Contract.

items.text: Do not press for immediate consummation; allow a space of time between contract and marriage for deliberation and inquiry.
items.quote: Betweene the Contract and Marriage, there ought to bee some certaine space or distance of time.

items.text: During that space, inquire whether there is any just cause that may hinder the marriage, and if found, remedy it.
items.quote: inquirie may be made, whether there be any iust cause, which may hinder the consummation of Marriage.

items.text: Have regard for honesty: do not seek to satisfy your fleshly desires right after the contract, but proceed with mature deliberation.
items.quote: persons espoused must haue regard of honestie, as well as of necessitie; not presently vpon the Contract, seeking to satisfie their own fleshly desires, after the manner of bruit beasts

items.text: Speak your promise of marriage in present-tense words and simply, without condition, to make the bond sure.
items.quote: The best manner of giuing this promise, is, to make it in words touching the present time, and simplie without any exception or condition expressed or conceiued.

items.text: Do not annex conditions that are impossible or dishonest to your marriage promise.
items.quote: conditions that are either impossible or dishonest, are not to bee accounted as promises annexed in way of Marriage.

items.text: Make your contract before fit and competent judges and witnesses.
items.quote: The Contract is a mention or mutuall promise of future mariage, before fit and competent Iudges and Witnesses.

items.text: If you have lain together before a condition is performed, do not use that condition to escape; the bond is sure.
items.quote: if the parties betrothed, do lie together before the condition ... be performed; then the contract for time to come is, without further controuersie, sure and certaine.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 13 · Of the Parent.

items.text: Nurse your own child at the breast and wrap it in swaddling clothes; only a just impediment excuses you to a nurse.
items.quote: the mother is her selfe to giue the infant sucke, and to wrap it vp in swadling clothes

items.text: Provide for your children meat, drink, and clothing; to refuse them necessary food is worse than an infidel.
items.quote: to prouide for his child meate, drinke, and clothing

items.text: When God gives ability and means, lay up something for your children's future maintenance; fathers ought to lay up for children, not children for fathers.
items.quote: for the children ought not to lay vp for the fathers, but the fathers for the children

items.text: Observe your child's inclination and natural gifts of body and mind, and bestow him in an honest calling and course of life suited to them.
items.quote: to obserue both the inclination, and the naturall gifts of bodie and mind that are in the child, and accordingly to bestow it in some honest calling & course of life

items.text: Consecrate to God those of your children with the most pregnant wit and best gifts, and bring them up in the study of the Scriptures to serve in the ministry.
items.quote: those of their children which haue the most pregnant wit, and be indued with the best gifts, be consecrated vnto God, and brought vp in the studie of the Scriptures

items.text: See that your child, as soon as may be after birth, is admitted into the true Church of God by baptism, and given a fit name.
items.quote: the child, so soone as may bee, after it is borne, bee admitted into the true Church of God by Baptisme, and haue a fit name giuen vnto it

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 5 · Of the choise of persons fit for Marriage.

items.text: Do not marry your brother or sister; such marriage is unlawful and forbidden.
items.quote: the mariages of brethren, and sisters are vnlawfull, and forbidden.

items.text: Do not marry your uncle or aunt, for they are in place of parents and near kin.
items.quote: these in regard of their inferiours, are in stead of parents, and therefore do come neare to the kindred of their flesh.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 5 · Of the choise of persons fit for Marriage.

items.text: Choose only a spouse of the opposite sex; the male is the superior sex and the female the inferior, made for procreation.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Chap. 5, Of the choise of persons fit for Marriage.
items.quote: The first is the distinction of the sex, which is either male, or female.

items.text: Do not marry any of your own flesh; abstain from all who are near of kin, especially in the right line which is forbidden without limit.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Chap. 5, Of the choise of persons fit for Marriage.
items.quote: No man shall come neare to any of the flesh of his flesh.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 10 · Of the Communion of married folkes, and of due beneuolence.

items.text: Communicate your person and goods to her for mutual help, necessity, and comfort.
items.quote: they do mutually and willingly communicate, both their persons, & goods each to other, for their mutuall helpe

items.text: Communicate your person and goods to him for mutual help, necessity, and comfort.
items.quote: they do mutually and willingly communicate, both their persons, & goods each to other, for their mutuall helpe

items.text: Love your wife as your own body, as Christ loved the church.
items.quote: So ought men to loue their wiues as their own bodies; he that loueth his wife, loueth himselfe.

items.text: Give due benevolence to your wife, not merely as courtesy but as a debt owed.
items.quote: Let the husband giue vnto the wife due beneuolence

items.text: Likewise give due benevolence to your husband, not merely as courtesy but as a debt owed.
items.quote: and likewise also the wife vnto the husband.

items.text: Use the marriage bed in a holy manner, with moderation, not with immoderate desire.
items.quote: that it be done in moderation. For euen in wedlocke excesse in lusts is no better then plaine adulterie before God.

items.text: Do not have sexual relations with your wife during her menstrual period.
items.quote: Thou shalt not go to a woman to vncouer her shame, as long as shee is put apart for her disease.

items.text: By mutual consent, abstain from sexual relations during a solemn fast to give yourselves to prayer.
items.quote: Defraud not one another, except it be with consent for a time, that you may giue your selues to fasting and prayer.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 12 · Of the Wife.

items.text: Submit yourself to your husband as the church is subject to Christ.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, ch. 12 Of the Wife
items.quote: The first is, to submit her selfe to her husband; and to acknowledge and reuerence him as her head in all things.

items.text: Acknowledge and reverence him as your head in all things.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, ch. 12 Of the Wife
items.quote: to acknowledge and reuerence him as her head in all things

items.text: Be obedient to him in all things, wholly depending on him in judgment and will, as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him Lord.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, ch. 12 Of the Wife
items.quote: The second dutie is, to be obedient vnto her husband in all things; that is, wholly to depend vpon him, both in iudgement and will.

items.text: Do not wander or stray abroad from your own house without your husband's knowledge and consent.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, ch. 12 Of the Wife
items.quote: the woman is not to take libertie of wandring, and straying abroad from her owne house, without the mans knowledge & cōsent.

items.text: Follow your husband when he moves or departs from place to place, unless he forsakes you or Christ.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, ch. 12 Of the Wife
items.quote: shee is to follow her husband, when hee flitteth or departeth from place to place, vnlesse hee forsake either her or Christ.

items.text: Do not be a cause of grief to your husband's parents.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, ch. 12 Of the Wife
items.quote: to be a cause of griefe to their kindred. Thus the proud wiues of Esau, the daughters of the Hittites, were a griefe of mind to Isaak and Rebekah.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 5 · Of the choise of persons fit for Marriage.

items.text: Do not marry your daughter-in-law, for she is as your own daughter.
items.quote: it is as well vnlawful for the father in law to marrie the daughter in law

items.text: Do not marry your mother-in-law, for she is as your own mother.
items.quote: the sonne in law to marry the mother in law

items.text: Do not marry your nephew's wife, for she is as a daughter to you.
items.quote: it is as vnlawful for the vncle by the mothers side, to marrie the wife of his sisters son
items.needs_role: nephew's wife (wife of one's sister's son)

items.text: Do not marry your deceased wife's sister, for she is as your own sister by affinity.
items.quote: it is in no sort lawful for a man, when his wife is dead, to marrie her sister

items.text: Do not take another wife beside her, for that would vex and dishonor her.
items.quote: he should greatly vex his first lawfull wife

items.text: Do not uncover your brother's shame by taking his wife.
items.quote: Thou shalt not discouer the shame of thy brothers wife; for it is thy brothers shame

items.text: Do not marry your wife's step-mother, for she is as a mother-in-law to you.
items.quote: the sonne in law may not marrie with his wiues step-mother

items.text: Do not marry your husband's step-father, for he is as a father-in-law to you.
items.quote: Neither may the daughter in law match with her husbands step-father

items.text: Do not marry your spouse's sibling's spouse, for you are as brother and sister to one another.
items.quote: my sisters husband may not marry my brothers wife

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 6 · Of consent in the Contract.

items.text: Do not make a private marriage contract without the free and lawful consent of your parents; honor your father and mother.
items.quote: Honor thy father and thy mother. Priuate contracts without free and lawfull consent of parents are meere nullities.

items.text: Yield free and full consent each to other; let no force or fear make the contract.
items.quote: The free and full consent of the parties, which is indeed the very soule and life of the contract.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 15 · Of the Master.

items.text: Choose servants who fear God and are willing to serve him, not merely strong or skillful hands.
items.quote: inquireth first after such as feare God, and be willing to serue him

items.text: Require only the labor their strength can bear, give them rest, and rule them not with cruelty but with pity and courtesy.
items.quote: enioyne them labour, and not to require more of them, then their strength will beare... yeeld them sometimes intercession & rest. Bee pitifull, bee courteous, one beare with another.

items.text: Give your servants their due portion of food and drink for the present.
items.quote: The good matron giueth the portion to her houshold, and the ordinary to her maids

items.text: Pay your servant his due wages in due time, and defraud him of no part of it.
items.quote: That the wages be proportionable to the work. That it be paid in due time, without deferring. That the seruant be not defrauded of any part of his due.

items.text: If your servant falls sick in your service, take all possible means to procure his recovery.
items.quote: if the seruant in time of his seruice be sicke, the masters care must be by all means possible to procure his recouery.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 8 · Of Mariage.

items.text: Bring your daughter to the bridegroom on her wedding day and give her to him.
items.quote: bring the Bride, and deliuer her to the Bride-groome

items.text: Do not marry without their consent; be ordered by them in betrothal.
items.quote: bound to be ordered, by their parents in the bestowing of themselues

items.text: Give or withhold consent to marriage only upon wise and just judgment, not rashly.
items.quote: not rashly, vnaduisedlie, or foolishlie, but out of good & wise consideration

items.text: Perform to her all matrimonial duties.
items.quote: performe each to other all matrimoniall duties

items.text: Perform to him all matrimonial duties.
items.quote: performe each to other all matrimoniall duties

items.text: Seek your guardian's consent for marriage, at least as a matter of honesty.
items.quote: their consent is not required of necessitie, but of honestie at least

items.text: Do not give your child in marriage to an ungodly or heretical person.
items.quote: denies to bestow his daughter... because hee knowes him to be an Arrian

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 10 · Of the Communion of married folkes, and of due beneuolence.

items.text: Do not reject your wife for barrenness; she is God's gift, and the fruit of the womb is his blessing.
items.quote: Hee therefore that in want of children, reiecteth his wife, whom he hath receiued at the hands of God, offereth wrong euen to God himselfe.

items.text: Maintain your superiority as head, even as you acknowledge her equal right to seek divorce for adultery.
items.quote: the man is to maintaine his superioritie, and the woman to obserue that modestie which beseemeth her towards the man.

items.text: Observe modesty and submission toward your husband, especially when seeking divorce.
items.quote: the man is to maintaine his superioritie, and the woman to obserue that modestie which beseemeth her towards the man.

items.text: Cherish each other as your own flesh, freely sharing goods, counsel, and labor for the preservation of both.
items.quote: they are freely to cōmunicate their goods, their coūsel, their labors each to other; for the good of themselues and theirs.

items.text: Rejoice in the wife of your youth; let her love delight you continually.
items.quote: Reioyce with the wife of thy youth... Let her be as the louing Hind, and pleasant wild goat: let her breasts satisfie thee at all times, and delight in her loue continually.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 5 · Of the choise of persons fit for Marriage.

items.text: Charge your children not to marry outside the faith, but to take spouses who are believers.
items.quote: thou shalt not take a wife vnto my son, of the daughters of the Cananites among whom I dwell

items.text: Keep faith with your betrothed; do not contract with another while your promise stands.
items.quote: the spouse by the bond of her promise to the man, becomes a wife

items.text: Do not put away your wife except for fornication; to do so and marry another is adultery.
items.quote: whosoeuer shall put away his wife, except it be for whoredome, & marieth another, committeth adulterie

items.text: If you depart, remain unmarried or be reconciled to your husband.
items.quote: if she depart, let her remaine vnmarried, or be reconciled vnto her husband

items.text: Do not put away your wife.
items.quote: let not the husband put away his wife

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 9 · Of the duties of married persons.

items.text: Do not separate yourself from your husband; dwell together with him.
items.quote: let not the wife separate her selfe from her husband

items.text: Do not forsake your wife; if she is willing to dwell with you, live together.
items.quote: If any brother haue an vnbeleeuing wife, and she be content to dwell with him, let him not forsake her

items.text: Dwell with her as a man of knowledge, giving her honor as the weaker vessel, remembering you are joint heirs of the grace of life, so your prayers be not hindered.
items.quote: giuing honor to the woman as to the weaker vessell, euen as they which are heires together of the grace of life, that your prayers be not interrupted

items.text: In the first year of marriage, do not go to war or be charged with business; be free at home and rejoice with your wife.
items.quote: he shall not go on warfare, neither shall be charged with any busines, but shall bee free at home one yeare, & reioyce with his wife

items.text: Do not desert one another without a just and necessary cause.
items.quote: Desertion is, when one of the married folkes, vpon a wilfull, and obstinate mind of their owne head, departeth from the other, without a iust, and necessarie cause

items.text: Even if one spouse has a contagious disease, continue dwelling together.
items.quote: Both the mariage it selfe, and the dutie of dwelling together, ought to continue firme and sure notwithstanding

items.text: If your spouse has a contagious disease, do not desire bodily union, lest you bring infection on yourself, your children, and the commonwealth; if you cannot abstain, pray to God for continence.
items.quote: the sound partie neither may, nor ought in good conscience, to desire coniunction with the other, whereby he, or she may bring infection vpon themselues

items.text: Before treating a desertion as dissolving the marriage, use all good means to bring the deserter to repentance.
items.quote: All good meanes must bee first vsed to bring the infected partie to repentance

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 7 · Of Reiection, or Refusall of the Contract.

items.text: Do not suddenly renounce the contract; allow time for amendment before declaring it void.
items.quote: a couenāt once made, is not suddenly to bee renounced... some longer respite is to be taken from the time of the contract

items.text: When a non-contagious but incurable disease makes mutual company loathsome, do not claim your marital right; surrender it by mutual consent.
items.quote: not to claime their right, but willingly to surrender it each to other by mutuall consent, that they may be free againe

items.text: Do not renounce the contract for a disease that is curable or does not disable you from marriage.
items.quote: yet this is not a sufficient cause to moue them to renounce, and dissolue the contract.

items.text: If you have voluntarily absented yourself, return and stand to your promise to marry your contracted spouse unless you can plead a just cause.
items.quote: he shall be forced by the Magistrates authoritie to stand to his promise, and take the woman for his wife.

items.text: If your contracted partner is detained against their will, wait for their return or for certain news of death before marrying another.
items.quote: expect his returne, or haue certaine notice of his death, before she promise, or haue to do with any other in way of mariage.

items.text: Before dissolving the contract for madness, try all good means and allow sufficient time for restoration.
items.quote: it is fit that all good meanes be tried and vsed, and sufficient time be giuen for the restoring of the diseased

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 13 · Of the Parent.

items.text: Sow the seeds of godliness and religion in the child's heart from the first use of reason, and ensure growth in knowledge and grace.
items.quote: sow the seeds of godlinesse and religion in the heart of the child, so soone as it comes to the vse of reason and vnderstanding

items.text: Call upon the child to remember the vow and promise made in baptism when he comes of age.
items.quote: the vow and promise made in Baptisme, which parents are bound to call vpon the child to remember

items.text: Rehearse God's commandments continually to your children and talk of them in the house.
items.quote: Thou shalt rehearse these words which I command thee continually to thy children

items.text: When your son asks the meaning of God's testimonies, ordinances, and laws, explain to him the Lord's works and deliverance.
items.quote: When thy sonne shall aske thee... thou shalt say vnto thy sonne; We were Pharaohs bondmen in Egypt

items.text: Correct the child with reproof and the rod when he does amiss, and do not leave him at liberty.
items.quote: The rod and correction giue wisdome, but a child set at libertie makes his mother ashamed

items.text: Govern the child without provoking him to anger by over-severity, and without failing to correct him as Eli did.
items.quote: Parents prouoke not your children to anger

items.text: When your child is fit for marriage and lacks continence, provide a suitable match or at least advise them to marry.
items.quote: he that giueth her to mariage, doth well

items.text: In arranging marriage, prefer piety and wisdom in the prospective spouse over beauty and riches.
items.quote: haue a greater respect vnto pietie and wisedome, then vnto beautie and riches

items.text: Do not force your child to marry a particular person; obtain their consent, as Rebekah's parents did.
items.quote: they first called her and asked her consent

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 8 · Of Mariage.

items.text: Do not give yourself in marriage without the free consent of your parents.
items.quote: the consent of the two parties is not sufficient, no not though they haue had societie together, vnlesse they haue the free cō sent of their parents also.

items.text: Do not make a vow to the Lord without your father's approval.
items.quote: if her father disallow her, that is, giueth no approbation or consent vnto the vow made, it shall be of no value, and the Lord wil forgiue her, because her father consented not.

items.text: Leave your father and mother and cleave to your wife.
items.quote: the man, euen in respect of habitation, should leaue father and mother and cleaue to his wife

items.text: If you seduce a maiden, you must have her father's consent to marry; if he refuses, pay the dowry.
items.quote: If her father refuse to giue her to him, he shall pay money according to the dowrie of virgins

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 5 · Of the choise of persons fit for Marriage.

items.text: Do not marry any of the sixteen sorts of near kin forbidden in Leviticus 18, nor any of like degree.
items.quote: sixteene seuerall sorts of persons with whom mariage is forbidden. The first is the mother.

items.text: Do not contract marriage with one unfit for its physical use by impotence, incurable palsy, or deprivation of the parts of generation.
items.quote: it is vnlawful to make a contract with such a person, as is vnfit for the vse of mariage

items.text: Do not consent to or command an espousal of a child under age; such a contract is of no moment.
items.quote: though it should be done by consent, or cōmandement of Parents, yet it is of no moment

items.text: Do not make a binding espousal while both parties are under age; it is unlawful and void unless ratified after full age or consummated.
items.quote: that which is made betweene two persons that are vnder age, is to bee holden and accounted as vnlawfull

items.text: If you are of full age and your espoused is under age, wait patiently for the time of accomplishment.
items.quote: the partie that is of full age, ought to tarrie and expect the time

items.text: Do not break off a lawful espousal made before full age, but rest in expectation of its accomplishment.
items.quote: the vnder-aged may not break off consent, either before, or when they be come to perfect yeares

items.text: Do not promise marriage to one with a loathsome, incurably contagious disease such as leprosy or the French pox.
items.quote: a promise of mariage made betweene those, whereof the one hath a disease so lothsome, as that the other vpon good ground cannot possiblie endure familiar societie

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 18 · Of the Mistresse of the familie, or Goodwife of the house.

items.text: Help him in governing the family as his associate in office, authority, and counsel.
items.quote: she is the associate, not only in office and authoritie, but also in aduise, and counsell vnto him.

items.text: Govern the house as much as concerns her in her place.
items.quote: gouerne the house, as much as concerneth her, in her place.

items.text: Labor cheerfully in profitable employments for the good of those under her charge.
items.quote: She seeketh wooll, and flax, and laboureth cheerefully with her hands.

items.text: Appoint the maids their work and oversee them in it.
items.quote: by appointing her maids their worke, and ouerseeing them therein.

items.text: Order your children in wisdom, instructing and admonishing them as needed.
items.quote: By ordering her children and seruants in wisdome; partly by instruction, partly by admonition.

items.text: Order your servants in wisdom, instructing and admonishing them as needed.
items.quote: By ordering her children and seruants in wisdome; partly by instruction, partly by admonition.

items.text: Give the household their portion of food in due season.
items.quote: She riseth whiles it is yet night, and giueth the portiō, or meat to her houshold.

items.text: Do not dispose of the goods common to both of you without your husband's allowance, express or implicit.
items.quote: these shee may not bestow, without his allowance, either expresse or at least general and implicite.

items.text: Instruct and guide him in matters of religion and godliness as his helper.
items.quote: his mother was not only an helper, but also a teacher or instructer, and guide vnto his father in matters of religion & godlines.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 17 · Of the Master of the familie or goodman of the house.

items.text: Bear the chief stroke in the worship of God within your family: pray for and with your household, and instruct them in the holy Scriptures, that they may grow in knowledge.
items.quote: I and my household wil serue the Lord.

items.text: Bring your family to public worship on the Sabbath, ensure they behave themselves reverently, and after the service examine them on what they have heard, that they may profit in knowledge and obedience.
items.quote: to looke that they do religiously there behaue themselues, and after the publike exercises ended, to take account of that which they haue heard

items.text: Provide food, drink, and clothing for your family, and see that they may live a quiet and peaceable life.
items.quote: to prouide for his family meat, drinke and clothing, and that they may liue a quiet & peaceable life

items.text: Keep order and exercise discipline in your house: for lesser faults use private admonition and correction; for capital crimes bring the offender to the civil magistrate; if private means fail, bring him to the church's censure; and if a servant remains incorrigible, remove him from the house.
items.quote: Correct thy sonne, and he will giue thee rest

items.text: Show hospitality to strangers, especially to Christians and ministers of the Word, giving them entertainment and lodging.
items.quote: Giuing your selues to hospitalitie. Be not forgetfull to lodge strangers.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 9 · Of the duties of married persons.

items.text: Keep wedlock by dwelling with your spouse and performing the duties of marriage; do not desert one another.
items.quote: the faultie person, who is the cause of this desertion, is to be forced by course of Ciuill, and Ecclesiasticall censure, to performe his, or her dutie.

items.text: Do not deal spitefully with your spouse; require no intolerable conditions, and do not neglect to relieve them in danger or extremity.
items.quote: Malicious dealing is, when dwelling together, they require each of other intolerable conditions: and when the one doth not regard nor relieue the other, being in danger or extremity

items.text: If your spouse deserts without cause, wait patiently, pray earnestly, and use all lawful means to reclaim them.
items.quote: the other must in patience, & earnest prayer vnto God, waite the time, vntill his mind may be changed

items.text: If you have caused your spouse to depart by just fear or fault, remain solitary until you are willing to do your duty.
items.quote: the delinquent partie is to remaine solitarie, till they be instructed and made willing to doe their duties

items.text: Defend your wife from danger that comes from strangers.
items.quote: If from a stranger, then the husband either takes vpon him the defence of his belieuing wife, or not; if he doth, then she ought to abide with him.

items.text: If you depart from your spouse for safety or conscience, do not forsake them finally; leave only for a time.
items.quote: She forsakes him not finally, but leaues him for a time.

items.text: Wait for your absent husband's return until you have certain knowledge of his death, unless his absence is malicious.
items.quote: the wife must rest in expectation of his returne, till she hath notice of his death

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 11 · Of the Husband.

items.text: Love her even as yourself.
items.quote: Let euery one loue his wife euen as himselfe.

items.text: Protect her from danger.
items.quote: he is the couering of thine eies amongst all that are with thee

items.text: Regard her estate as your own and provide maintenance for her, both during your life and after your death as far as you can.
items.quote: he that loueth his wife loueth himselfe; For no man yet hated his owne flesh, but nourisheth it

items.text: Honor her.
items.quote: Giving honor to the woman.

items.text: Make account of her as your companion and yoke-fellow, not as ruler or servant.
items.quote: out of his side, to the end that man should take her as his mate.

items.text: Bear patiently with her weaknesses and infirmities, as the weaker vessel.
items.quote: Giving honor to the woman, as vnto the weaker vessell

items.text: Allow yourself to be admonished or advised by her when she counsels rightly.
items.quote: in all that Sarah shall say vnto thee, heare her voice

items.text: Correct her only by word of reproof and admonition; never beat or strike her.
items.quote: He may reproue & admonish her in word only... But hee may not chastise her either with stripes, or stroks.

items.text: If she is desperately perverse, bear it patiently as the cross God has laid on you, and do not take vengeance.
items.quote: must beare it, if it may be borne, as the portion of his crosse laid vpon him by God.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 5 · Of the choise of persons fit for Marriage.

items.text: Do not marry your aunt (father's sister, mother's sister) or your uncle's wife; God expressly forbids it as uncovering near kin's nakedness.
items.quote: God by expresse law forbiddeth mariage with the aunt, the fathers sister ... and with the mothers sister ... and with the fathers brother wife

items.text: Though marriage between cousins is lawful, avoid it when it would give offense, hinder broader alliances, or violate modesty toward near kindred.
items.quote: the modestie that ought to be in those which intend mariage, auoideth as much as may be, these and such like coniunctions

items.text: Do not marry your child to a near cousin if it is inexpedient or would cause offense; remember all things lawful are not expedient.
items.quote: though it were in it selfe lawfull, being no where forbidden by God, yet in sundrie respects being inexpedient, it ought not to bee done

items.text: After your spouse dies, do not marry his or her parent or other near affine; the prohibition of affinity remains to preserve public honesty.
items.quote: the same alliance ceaseth and determineth vpon the death of either partie espoused or maried; yet so as the prohibition of coniunction remaines, and stands in force

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 5 · Of the choise of persons fit for Marriage.

items.text: Do not marry a woman of vastly different age, lest you be unable to fulfill marital duties or expose her to temptation.
items.quote: when a man of great yeares matcheth with a woman very yong ... the elder partie ... may the sooner come to be vnfit for mariage duties

items.text: Do not marry a man of vastly different age, for the elder may become unfit for marital duties and the younger tempted to unchastity.
items.quote: or a yong stripling marrieth an aged woman; the elder partie growing weake and impotent, may the sooner come to be vnfit for mariage duties; and the yonger ... in danger of incontinencie.

items.text: Marry only a woman of your own social condition, lest inequality bring confusion and disturbance to your household.
items.quote: the Prince, the Noble man, the free-man, the gentleman, the yeoman, &c. should be ioyned in societie with them, that are of the same or like condition with themselues, and not otherwise.

items.text: Marry only a man of your own social condition, lest inequality bring confusion and disturbance to your household.
items.quote: should be ioyned in societie with them, that are of the same or like condition with themselues, and not otherwise.

items.text: Do not betroth a woman who has been deflowered or is accused of adultery, and especially not one you yourself have defiled, for it is unlawful and shameful.
items.quote: a cōtract made with such a one, as himself hath before deflowred, is by the law of God vnlawfull.

items.text: Do not marry a man who keeps a concubine unless he renounces her and repents, for by marrying him you consent to his adultery.
items.quote: it is altogether inexpedient, that a woman should be married to such a man, as hath a Concubine, vnlesse he formerly renounce her, and testifie the same by true and vnfeined repentance.

items.text: Do not marry a harlot, a defamed woman, or one of infamous parents, for it is reproachful to your household and to the Christian profession.
items.quote: ought to take to himselfe in mariage a harlot, a defamed woman, or one that comes of infamous parents

items.text: Do not contract with the sister of the woman already affianced to you, for it is not meet.
items.quote: it is not meete for a man to be contracted to the sister of her that is alreadie affianced vnto him.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 16 · Of the Seruant.

items.text: Be subject to your master and please him in all things, not answering back.
items.quote: Let seruants be subiect to their masters, and please them in all things, not answering againe.

items.text: Serve him faithfully and diligently, as unto Christ, even if he is harsh.
items.quote: Seruants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with feare & trembling, in singlenes of your hearts, as vnto Christ.

items.text: Do his business not negligently or with eye-service; be trustworthy and do not steal or deceive.
items.quote: hee be trustie & withhold his hands from picking, and his heart from deceiuing his master.

items.text: Pay a hired servant his wages justly.
items.quote: To him belongs the iust paiment of his hire

items.text: If you must correct a servant, do it with moderation, respect his age, and treat him as a son.
items.quote: respect bee had vnto his age, and the correction be vsed with moderation, as if hee were his sonne.

items.text: Do not take the power of life and death over a bond-servant; that belongs to the magistrate.
items.quote: the master haue not ouer his seruant the power of life and death; for this takes away the lawful power of the Magistrate
items.conflict: Slavery conflicts with the equality of all persons in Christ (Gal 3:28) and the command to love neighbor as self.

items.text: Do not use a bond-servant at your own will in all things; if you injure him, set him free.
items.quote: libertie granted him, to vse his seruant at his owne will and pleasure in all things
items.conflict: Slavery conflicts with the equality of all persons in Christ (Gal 3:28) and the command to love neighbor as self.

items.text: Do not command a servant anything against piety or justice; obey God rather than men.
items.quote: the power be not enlarged to the commanding of things against piety or iustice; for in these cases a man must rather obey God then man

items.text: Do not separate married bond-servants from each other, or parents from their children.
items.quote: masters do not take libertie to make separation of those their seruants that be married, the one from the other, or of those that be parents from their children

items.text: Do not transfer a bond-servant to an ungodly or unbelieving master, lest he be led away from the true religion.
items.quote: masters do not take libertie to put ouer their seruants to vngodly and vnbelieuing masters

items.text: Do not bind a bond-servant to perpetual slavery; let him go free unless he willingly chooses to stay.
items.quote: they do not bind them to perpetuall slauery, & neuer make them free.
items.conflict: Slavery conflicts with the equality of all persons in Christ (Gal 3:28) and the command to love neighbor as self.

items.text: Do not procure or retain servitude by force; it is worse than spoiling riches.
items.quote: the seruitude be not procured and retained by force; for it is a more grieuous crime to spoile a man of his libertie, then of his riches.
items.conflict: Slavery conflicts with the equality of all persons in Christ (Gal 3:28) and the command to love neighbor as self.

work: Christian Oeconomie: or, A Short Survey of the Right Manner of Erecting and Orde
heading: A SHORT SVRVEY OF THE RIGHT MANNER OF ERECTING and ordering a Familie, according to the Scriptures. · Chapter 14 · Of the Sonne.

items.text: Obey your parents, whether natural or step-parents, as long as you live.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 14, Of the Sonne
items.quote: First to yeeld them obedience, whether they be his naturall parents or otherwise, as his step-father & step-mother, and that while he liueth.

items.text: Obey your parents-in-law; accept their counsel and commands as from those in parental authority.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 14, Of the Sonne
items.quote: Moses father in law said vnto him, Heare now my voice... Ruth said vnto Naomi her mother in law, All that thou biddest me, I wil do.

items.text: Submit to your parents' direction in choosing your lawful calling; be ordered and appointed by their discretion.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 14, Of the Sonne
items.quote: in the choyce of a lawfull calling, wherein the child is to be ordered and appointed at the discretion of the parent.

items.text: Let your parents be principal agents in your marriage; do not dissent from their advice without weighty cause, and by dutiful conduct seek to mitigate any harshness.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 14, Of the Sonne
items.quote: the parent is the principall agent and disposer of the child.

items.text: Obey your parents in all domestic labours, so that you may be skillful in household affairs.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 14, Of the Sonne
items.quote: the daughters: They must yeeld obedience to their parents in all Domesticall labours, that they may be skilfull in houshold affaires.

items.text: Recompense your parents' love and care by relieving them in their need with food, clothing, and other necessities.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 14, Of the Sonne
items.quote: to recompence his fathers loue, and care ouer him, by relieuing him in case of want, if God giue abilitie, with food and rayment, and other necessaries.

items.text: Do not strike or curse your father or mother; you must not ill-use them in word or deed.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 14, Of the Sonne
items.quote: if the sonne neglecteth them, and doth the contrarie, by ill vsage of his parent, either in word or deed, he is worthie of death.

items.text: Give your firstborn son a double portion of your goods, as is his right by perpetual law, except in case of notorious wickedness.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 14, Of the Sonne
items.quote: He shall acknowledge the son of the hated for the first borne, & giue him a double portion of all that he hath.
items.conflict: Ceremonial law, fulfilled in Christ; not a binding ordinance for Christian families.

items.text: Do not make a vow without your parent's consent; such a vow is not binding, and your parent may make it void.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 14, Of the Sonne
items.quote: A vow so made is not of force to bind the child, but by the Law of nature & common equitie, is to be made void.

items.text: In remarrying, seek your parents' consent; though not strictly required, it is fitting and honors them.
items.citation: Christian Oeconomie, Ch. 14, Of the Sonne
items.quote: Consent in this case, though it be not absolutely necessarie, yet it is to be thought fit and conuenient, because children owe dutie of honor.
